ai.description: This 5–6 cm frog is golden-yellow to brown with a distinct dark lateral stripe. It features a pointed snout, long slender limbs, and prominent dorsolateral folds. It belongs to the family Ranidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana flavescens* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent cream-colored dorsolateral fold that contrasts sharply with its dark flanks.
ai.habitat: *Hylarana flavescens* inhabits moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at mid-to-high altitudes of 800–1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Yellowish Golden-backed Frog is primarily nocturnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates along the moist forest floor and near stream banks at night.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana flavescens* breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying large clutches of gelatinous eggs in stagnant forest pools or slow-moving streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hylarana flavescens* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting evergreen forests at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Hylarana flavescens* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, pulsed notes emitted from the edges of forest streams and marshy areas.
